messages:
Riley Gomez: POC with Atlas Retail: /v1/embeddings returns 403 'insufficient scope' but /v1/health is 200. They say token is a service account.
Priya Nair: paste minimal request and blacked claims if possible.
Riley Gomez: request header: Authorization: Bearer <token>. They also send X-Env: ci-runner. Body is standard. Response: 403 {
  "error": "insufficient_scope_or_missing_project"
}
Kai Zhou: common culprits: claim name mismatch (project vs project_id), scope naming (embeddings vs embeddings.read), or token minted for wrong org.
Riley Gomez: customer shared claims: {sub: svc-atlas, org: atlas, project_id: atlas-poc, scopes: ["embeddings"]}. Aha project_id not project.
presales-bot: Tip: API requires a 'project' claim or trusted proxy to inject x-project. Console can map project_id but tokens used by API must include 'project'.
infra-oncall: I can quickly add a compatibility acceptance for project_id for 48h but recommend they change generator. Also adding a clearer error string to help debug.
Priya Nair: ask them to re-issue token with project: atlas-poc and retry. Also verify scope is one of the allowed forms.
Riley Gomez: they re-issued with project present and embeddings succeeded. They mentioned earlier their CI runner strips x-project header so relying on header injection was flaky.
Kai Zhou: noted for KB: POC auth checklist: 1) ensure token has 'project' claim, 2) confirm scope naming, 3) avoid relying on mutable headers from CI/runners, 4) check quota if x-rate-hint appears.
Riley Gomez: adding KB entry and updating POC ticket. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
